punchline: Air Force strategist John Boyd told young officers they'd have to choose between being somebody and doing something.
thirty_sec: John Boyd was an Air Force pilot whose ideas shaped a generation of American fighter planes. He told promising young officers they'd hit a fork in the road. Go along with the system and collect promotions. Or do the work that matters, even if it annoys your bosses and costs you rank. Boyd took the second road. His ideas had a huge impact, and he never made it past colonel.
question: Have you ever had to choose between getting the credit and doing the work you actually cared about?
